target: new: conjunction of two values in a hyphenated compound
reason: Two hair qualities that hold together: floccose (PATO_0104366) and tomentose (PATO_0002341). 'Stellate' describes the hairs and would need a quality of a trichome part. This is a conjunction, not a single value or a continuum.
'Inequidistant' spines or leaflets are not evenly spaced. FLOPO:0991365 has 'equidistant' as a synonym.

Ironbark is the hard, dark, deeply furrowed bark of some Eucalyptus. The fissured surface is what it shares with bark descriptions in other floras. Its kino impregnation and hardness are too genus-specific to justify a separate class.
'Lumpy' only strengthens the wrinkled surface. The 'stone' in the examples is the endocarp.
In botanical_colour_synonyms.tsv, 'buff', 'pale buff' and 'grayish buff' are all NARROW synonyms of orange yellow. The phrase is the same head word with degree modifiers.
A pseudospicate inflorescence looks like a spike without being one, which matches the definition of spike-like/spiciform.

target: comparison or relation stated without its second term
reason: In ferns, 'conform' means similar to the lateral pinnae. It is a comparison like 'similar', which the previous review rejected, and it is usually written without the part it compares with.

target: new: conjunction of two values in a hyphenated compound
reason: Two values that hold together: elliptic (PATO_0000947, synonym ellipsoid) and asymmetrical (PATO_0000616). No single term is needed.
The widest part of a leaf or lobe is towards the apex, which is the obovate class of plane shapes. The extreme of 'at the apex' itself is lost.

target: new: conjunction of two values in a hyphenated compound
reason: The margin is toothed (PATO_0001205 dentated) and ciliate (PATO_0001408 ciliated). These are two attributes, not one value.

target: new: conjunction of two values in a hyphenated compound
reason: Two hair qualities that hold together: villous (FLOPO:0991051) and ciliated (PATO_0001408), the latter usually on the margin.
A 'clean bole' is a trunk without branches over its length. Only applies with the bearer stem/bole (PO_0009047).
Tertiary nerves or stigma lobes are parallel to each other, so this is 'parallel to' (PATO_0002272) towards the other members of the set. 'Closely' is a degree modifier.

target: new: conjunction of two values in a hyphenated compound
reason: Cylindrical (PATO_0001873) and flattened (PATO_0002254) hold together. This is not a continuum between them.

target: new: conjunction of two values in a hyphenated compound
reason: Setose (PATO_0002289) and glandular (PATO_0002117). 'Densely' is a degree modifier. Too few statements to justify a class beside FLOPO:0991172 stipitate-glandular.
The previous review mapped lepidote to scaly. The fringed margin (PATO_0002311 fimbriated) belongs to the scales, not to the bearer, and is too rare for a sibling of FLOPO:0991304 stellate-lepidote.
'Flushed' means tinged with a colour, so the colour value is grey. The tinge is degree information that stays in the record.
'Glochidiate' is a RELATED synonym of barbed. 'Tipped' only places the barbs at the apex.
Lentil-shaped means lenticular, which the previous review mapped to biconvex.
A size relative to an unstated norm, between medium-sized and large. It cannot be told apart from FLOPO:0991032 medium-sized or PATO_0000586 increased size.
A negated statement about distribution ('not restricted to the apices'). It states no quality of the part.
In botanical_colour_synonyms.tsv, 'plum' is a NARROW synonym of FLOPO:0988028.
Spanish 'corteza cuarteada' is bark cracked into squarish plates, which is the chequered pattern of tessellated. The lenticel example fits less well.

target: new: conjunction of two values in a hyphenated compound
reason: Pubescent (PATO_0000455) and red hairs: the colour (PATO_0000322) belongs to the trichomes, not to the bearer.
The lobes are themselves divided again. Read on the lobe as bearer (PO_0025517), that is the split quality.
Here 'semi-' works like 'sub-' or '±': decumbent (PATO_0002343) with the qualifier approximately.

target: condition of the specimen, not a quality
reason: The examples describe old or decayed leaves reduced to their veins, i.e. damage or age rather than a heritable phenotype.
PATO_0001890 is defined as being divided into three branches, with synonym trifurcate. The previous review mapped 'dichotomous' to bifurcated in the same way.

target: new: conjunction of two values in a hyphenated compound
reason: Transparent (PATO_0000964, synonym hyaline) and tinged brown (FLOPO:0988003 brown). One is an optical quality and the other a colour.
A transcription error for 'cuneate' (c read as e), shown by 'euneate at the base'. Better fixed in the transcription than kept as a lexicon entry.
